 EXPERTS EXPECT BUSY ROADS AND CROWDED FLIGHTS FOR HOLIDAYS
 Experts expect busy roads and crowded flights for holidays
 Share 
 Print
 JACK DEWITT 
 | Hagadone News Network 
 | UPDATED 3 hours, 35 minutes AGO
 A Washington Dept. of Transportation snow plow works on a stretch of eastbound Interstate Highway 90, Thursday, Dec. 9, 2021, as snow falls near Snoqualmie Pass in Washington state. More U.S. drivers could find themselves stuck on snowy highways or have their travel delayed this winter due to a shortage of snowplow drivers as some states are having trouble finding enough people willing to take the jobs. (AP Photo/Ted S. Warren)
 by 
 JACK DEWITT 
 Staff Writer 
 | 
 November 17, 2026 1:07 AM 
 Experts forecast busy roads and packed planes in the coming months. To help you manage packed schedules and holiday traffic, local travel experts shared tips to make your journey as smooth as possible. 
 Spokane International Airport projects that 165,000 passengers are expected to arrive and depart over the coming week, up almost 5% from last year, according to a press release. 
 “Whether you’re taking a road trip or flying, you’ll have plenty of company as everyone tries to make it in time for turkey and all the trimmings,” said Dave Haring, Spokane International Airport CEO, in a Monday press release.  
 Officials expect the airport to be busiest from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. They estimate nearly 3,500 passengers will arrive and depart during that time. Other high-traffic periods will occur from 5 to 7 a.m. and between 9 and 11 p.m.
 Access to the airport’s main terminal curbside remains closed to both vehicles and pedestrians due to construction with the Spokane International Airport Expansion Project. 
 Drivers approaching the terminal can expect to be routed through a new two-lane bypass road to access their respective drop-off and pick-up locations. Pedestrians using the parking facilities can access the terminal through the skybridges. 
 Spokane International Airport made several travel recommendations to make the Airport easier: 
 • Arrive at the airport at least two hours before your scheduled boarding time. 
 • Avoid wrapped gifts and packages in checked and carry-on luggage. A wrapped gift may require TSA to unwrap it to inspect its contents. 
 • Arrive in the Cell Phone Waiting Lot when picking a passenger up. 
 • Ensure identification is REAL ID- compliant before leaving home. 
 AAA Idaho estimates similar road congestion. It estimates that 81.5 million Americans will pack the family car and take a road trip for Thanksgiving weekend, including 476,000 Idahoans. 
 While the travel numbers are actually down 0.1%, AAA Idaho public affairs director Matthew Conde said travelers won’t feel a difference.
 According to AAA, the top 10 Thanksgiving destinations for Idahoans are Las Vegas, Honolulu, Anaheim, Orlando, San Diego, Salt Lake City, Phoenix, Nashville, Bozeman, and New York.
 AAA says the worst days for travel are late Tuesday afternoon and the Wednesday before Thanksgiving. 
 The best day to leave? Thanksgiving Day. 
 AAA has made several recommendations to make the trip easier: 
 • Double-check your car battery, engine and tires before making the journey. It also recommends topping off fluid levels and inspecting engine hoses and belts. 
 • Keep a change of clothes, medications and important documents in your carry-on bag if you decide to fly. 
 • Download your airline’s app for updates. 
 • Bring TSA-approved food items with you to avoid expensive airport food. 
 Consider an airport farther from home that offers better flight deals.
 Idaho resident Alex Luna will drive to Seattle for Thanksgiving. He recommends making a travel plan "a week out" before traveling. 
 "We're thinking about it now, what we want do, what route we want to take, where we want to stop for gas, where we want to eat," Luna said. 
 His process includes checking for road construction, finding mountain passes and pinpointing the best gas price. He also noted that travelers should fill up before nearing a pass because the closer you get, the price goes up. 
 He also recommended a little car maintenance before setting off. 
 "I always get an oil change," he said. 
 Luna also cleans and checks his truck for unneeded items before leaving, removing any "dead weight" and giving him a comfortable place to sit for the trip. 
 "Nothing in the bed that's going to ruin my miles per gallon. Try to keep it light," he said.
